A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same frequency-filtering approach to membership inference attacks. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations on DDIM and Stable Diffusion, together with frequency analyses, ablations, and robustness experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds CLID evaluations, memorization-defense experiments, and membership-score normality tests.

M1.justification: The Fourier transform, frequency mask, inverse transform, and filtered-distance decision rule in Equations 9–11 remain unchanged. Evaluating the filter with CLID introduces no documented modification to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The same seven datasets and diffusion-image membership inference tasks remain covered. Caption-free and BLIP-caption scenarios already appeared in v1 Appendix E.6. The new memorization defense changes training controls within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix D.5, Table 12 adds evaluated CLID and CLID+F comparisons on Pokémon, MS-COCO, and Flickr under weaker overfitting. v1 cited the corresponding work but evaluated only Naive, SecMI, and PIA.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a Pokémon evaluation crossing augmentation on/off with SSei memorization mitigation on/off. The earlier augmentation-only evaluation across DDIM and three Stable Diffusion datasets is narrowed. Default splits, resolutions, batch sizes, training budgets, and attack metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Robustness evidence is substantially revised through new SSei defense comparisons and normality checks addressing the theoretical assumptions. v1's DDIM augmentation-removal analysis and corresponding MS-COCO/Flickr Stable Diffusion results disappear. Existing hyperparameter ablations, weaker-overfitting tests, and missing-caption analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix D.2 newly reports Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics, p-values, and a 0.05 significance threshold for member and hold-out scores on MS-COCO and Flickr. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals for attack performance.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores are retained, but v2 adds CLID, SSei-defense, and normality-test results while removing substantial augmentation results. Table 12 newly reports MS-COCO AUCs of 93.32/95.41 for CLID/CLID+F. Some overlapping controls change without explanation: Pokémon Naive AUC without augmentation is 86.45 in v1 Table 7 versus 87.95 in v2 Table 6.

T1.justification: v1's Gaussian-score Theorem 1, explicit error-function expression, and Appendix C derivation are removed. v2 replaces them with a cited relationship between the standard-deviation ratio and membership advantage. Proposition 1 and its proof are retained, while Appendix A.2 adds formal definitions for the evaluated memorization defense.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion broaden applicability wording from pixel-wise error-based attacks to error-based attacks, supported by the explicit extension to likelihood-based CLID. The central frequency-deficiency finding, filtering contribution, and negligible-overhead claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that normality tests validate the theoretical assumption and that filtering does not depend strongly on normality. It also discusses effectiveness against memorization defenses and broader attack families. The limitation concerning weak performance on pre-trained models is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly states that implementation and scripts are supplied in supplementary materials, with public release upon publication; v1 only promised release. Appendix A.2 describes the defense's sample-exclusion rule. Core hardware and tabulated training settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Coates et al. (2011) and Falck et al. (2025), removes the J. Li et al. (2024) black-box attack reference, and expands discussion of Wen et al.'s memorization defense. Attribution of the Gaussian membership-advantage relationship to Yeom et al. becomes more explicit.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with terminology edits, an explicit adversary-capabilities paragraph, reordered experimental subsections, and reorganized appendices. v2 adds an author, an LLM-use disclosure, and a reproducibility statement. These are limited editorial and structural revisions rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document template with revised title, author block, headings, and running headers. Tables are substantially reorganized: the constraint table moves to the appendix, defense conditions replace dataset columns, and normality and CLID tables are added. All nine figures retain their content, with placement and sizing changes.

improvement.justification: CLID and SSei evaluations modestly strengthen evidence for applicability beyond v1's three baselines and augmentation-only controls. The benefit is limited by removed augmentation evidence, overstated conclusions from normality tests, and new numerical inconsistencies. For example, v2 Table 18 reports a Naive gain of 42.01 although 46.00 minus 6.99 equals 39.01. These issues prevent a stronger improvement judgment.
